status: DRAFT — NOT FROZEN. Awaiting review of Experiment_Plan_v1.4_SmallToBig.md.
freeze_procedure: On acknowledgement, stamp frozen_utc and the SHA-256 hashes of the plan and the small-to-big source files, then commit BEFORE the first run. Deliberately not stamped yet: freezing is the act that should FOLLOW review, and freezing criteria nobody else has read is exactly how the v1.3 harm-branch gap happened.
amends: v1.1 base plan; independent of v1.2 (identity) and v1.3 (reranker)
axis: orthogonal retrieval-unit change — every condition scored with and without small-to-big from the same corpus and query set, paired per query. NOT a new condition.

headroom_analysis_before_hypothesis.measure: ceiling gap = 1 - recall@10 — the share of queries whose gold is not retrieved at all, which is the pool small-to-big can address
headroom_analysis_before_hypothesis.conclusion: Track A cannot express a success criterion for this treatment; Track B can. Primary hypothesis is therefore scoped to Track B BEFORE any run, with Track A as a no-harm check.

decides_on: Track B (150 queries, all test — dev_fraction 0.0). Track A (176 test queries) secondary.

conditions_excluded.C1: semantic chunker already sets its own boundaries
conditions_excluded.C3_C5: units are already marker-delimited, making 'child of a marked section' partly circular

C0.child: naive cut of raw text at child_tokens

C2.child: naive cut of raw text at child_tokens
C2.parent: enclosing naive chunk + its contextual blurb

C4.child: naive cut of FORMATTED text at child_tokens

no_sweep_rationale: Track B has no dev split (dev_fraction 0.0), so sweeping child size there would contaminate the test set, and transferring a Track-A-swept size would be an untested assumption. Both sizes are pre-declared and both reported; no post-hoc selection between them.
provenance_rule_MANDATORY: Hits are scored on the CHILD's source_ranges — the unit retrieval actually found — NEVER on the parent's. Scoring on parent ranges would mechanically increase overlap with any gold span, rewarding dilution: the widest parent would always win. The parent is attached as a separate context field and is never passed to hit_flags. A test must assert that widening the parent leaves every recall number unchanged.
declared_structural_advantage: For C4 the parent is a semantically coherent formatter-marked section; for C0/C2 it is an arbitrary 768-token window. If C4 outperforms, part of that is the formatter supplying better parent boundaries — a real property of the treatment, but not the same claim as 'small-to-big helps'. The primary hypothesis is within-condition (X+s2b vs X), which is immune to this. Declared here rather than left for a reviewer to find.
measures_retrieval_half_only: This tests whether smaller indexed children find gold that current units miss. The generation-side benefit of returning coherent parent context is ASSERTED, NOT MEASURED — the harness has no generation metric.

hypotheses.H7: primary, Track B: for each X in {C0,C2,C4}, X+small-to-big recall@5 > X at child_tokens=128, paired, CI excludes 0 after Holm
hypotheses.H7a: secondary, Track A: no-harm check — small-to-big does not significantly REDUCE recall@5. Track A is not expected to gain
hypotheses.H7b: robustness: H7 at child_tokens=256, reported alongside 128, no selection after the fact
hypotheses.H7c: descriptive: parent context-sufficiency rate and mean parent token count. Inflation-prone by construction; NO decision weight; never quoted as a recall number

decision_rules.ADOPT: H7 significant positive on Track B at child_tokens=128 (paired CI excludes 0 after Holm within {C0,C2,C4}) AND H7a shows no significant harm on Track A
decision_rules.ADOPT_SCOPED: H7 significant positive confined to a PRE-NAMED admissible scope. Admissible scopes, declared now: (a) one condition family — C0/C2 versus C4; (b) one child size but not the other. Any other scope is a hypothesis, not a verdict
decision_rules.KILL: H7 effect not statistically distinguishable from zero on Track B
decision_rules.REJECT_HARM: significant NEGATIVE effect on any primary condition on EITHER track — same rule as ADOPT with the sign reversed

branch_precedence: REJECT_HARM takes precedence over KILL when both could apply; a harm finding is reported as harm, never as a null
harm_reporting_rule: a significant negative is reported in the direction it fell, with the same prominence a positive would receive
harm_branch_motivation: v1.3 froze ADOPT/ADOPT_SCOPED/KILL only, then produced a significant negative that fitted none of them and had to be recorded as 'REJECT (criteria incomplete)'. Small-to-big can plausibly harm: smaller units carry less context and may embed worse.
holm_families: H7's three Track B conditions form one family. Track A's no-harm checks form a SEPARATE family. Neither is merged with v1.1's H1-H4 or v1.3's H6. Child-size variants are reported separately, never pooled.
one_shot_rule: if H7 fails, changing child size, parent definition or embedder and re-testing on this same Track A/B split is NOT a fresh test; a retry needs a new pre-registered amendment stating what changed and why
reporting_rule: H7c and any interaction are reported in whichever direction they fall; a result unfavourable to small-to-big or to the formatter is reported with equal prominence

environment_pins.comparability_note: v1.1's published numbers used all-MiniLM-L6-v2. v1.4 pins bge-base, so v1.4 absolute numbers are comparable to v1.3's, NOT to v1.1's. Only within-run paired deltas are quotable across amendments.

run_requirements.pipefail: no result-bearing command may run through a pipe that can mask its exit status (template §A1)

not_tested: generation quality or faithfulness with parent context (no generation metric)
